findings.claim: This diff makes 'permissions' a votable proposals kind (proposals.go:39 kindDimension), and the smine-permissions skill writes its single group title 'Allowlist additions' verbatim in English on the stated contract that the title is 'translated in the UI'. germanCatalog has no entry for either 'permissions' or 'Allowlist additions', so on a German profile proposals.html:30 ({{t .File.Kind}}) and :60 ({{t .Title}}) fall through translate()'s identity path and render the English engine terms as the page's section heading and group title. Item correctness-11 (navigation and page headings render in German for the casual German user) fails for this section, and so does the skill-to-UI translation contract.
findings.evidence: Re-read i18n.go in full (lines 8-122): the catalog covers skills, workflows, context, routines, rules, actions, facts, acdsl, New skills, Edits to existing skills, Workflows (skill-bundled scripts) and Considered, not proposed, but has no 'permissions' or 'Allowlist additions' key. translate() (i18n.go:124-132) returns the key unchanged when it is missing. Re-read proposals.html:30 (<h2>{{t .File.Kind}}) and :60 ({{t .Title}}) and proposals.go:37-42 (the new permissions entry in kindDimension, which makes the kind votable through handleProposalVote:614). git grep on skills/smine/smine-permissions/SKILL.md, line 62: 'Single group: Allowlist additions. This title is a machine-read key — always written verbatim in English regardless of any presentation-profile language'. Line 32: 'the fixed group title (machine-read key, translated in the UI)'. skills/smine/smine/SKILL.md:48 runs smine-permissions in the default parallel dimension set, writing proposals/permissions.json. Trigger: a German presentation profile (language: de) plus any nightly run in which smine-permissions emits at least one proposal. /proposals then shows the headings 'permissions' and 'Allowlist additions' in English. Not in the known ledger, whose only permissions-kind row is the untested harness-friction dimension.

findings.fix: Start the wrapper in its own process group (SysProcAttr Setpgid on unix, a job object or tree kill on Windows) and set cmd.Cancel to kill the whole group, so the 6h deadline stops the stage's claude children before running flips to false.
findings.claim: The 6h bootstrap backstop kills only the wrapper bash. exec.CommandContext's default cancel sends SIGKILL to cmd.Process alone, and the script is `exec bash "$1"`, so that pid is the cmd/bootstrap/run.sh shell. The stage children it started through routine_run_claude (claude -p …) are not signalled and keep running, reparented to launchd. Wait() then returns, and the goroutine sets s.bootstrap.running = false, which reopens the concurrency guard at bootstrap.go:47 while the orphaned stage is still mining or applying. A second bootstrap can then start alongside it. The 6h deadline that spec-9 (correctness-93) carries over unchanged therefore never bounds the actual claude work.
findings.evidence: Re-read bootstrap.go:78-104 in full. runCtx carries context.WithTimeout(…, bootstrapDeadline). cmd is exec.CommandContext(runCtx, bashPath, "-c", verifyPathPrefix+`exec bash "$1"`, "bash", "cmd/bootstrap/run.sh"). No SysProcAttr process group and no cmd.Cancel override are set: shell.HideWindow is a no-op on non-Windows (internal/shell/hide_other.go:9), and only CreationFlags/HideWindow on Windows. A git grep for Setpgid/Setsid in cmd/ and internal/ finds nothing. On expiry Go calls Process.Kill (SIGKILL to the single pid), and SIGKILL of a parent does not reach its children. With Stdout/Stderr set to an *os.File, Wait returns as soon as that pid exits, and the goroutine (lines 97-104) clears running. Trigger: any bootstrap run whose stages are still active 6h after spawn. Exposure is 'eventually' because the frequency of runs longer than 6h cannot be shown from the code. Not in the known ledger, whose bootstrap.go rows are the log location/pid, tests, style, and the error-message wording.
